facts.statement: Avisaurus is a genus of enantiornithine birds from the Late Cretaceous of North America.
facts.quote: Avisaurus (meaning "bird lizard") is a genus of enantiornithine avialan from the Late Cretaceous of North America.

facts.statement: Avisaurus was a large enantiornithine, with the species A. darwini weighing up to 1.2 kg and A. archibaldi weighing up to 1.7 kg.
facts.quote: Avisaurus was a large enantiornithine, with A. darwini weighing up to 1.2 kg and A. archibaldi weighing up to 1.7 kg.

facts.statement: The holotype of Avisaurus archibaldi was collected in 1975 in Garfield County, Montana, USA.
facts.quote: It was collected in 1975 in the UCMP locality V73097, in Garfield County, Montana, USA.

facts.statement: The holotype of Avisaurus archibaldi is a single fossil tarsometatarsus held by the University of California Museum of Paleontology.
facts.quote: The holotype is represented by a single fossil of a tarsometatarsus in the collection of the University of California Museum of Paleontology.

facts.statement: The species name archibaldi honors J. David Archibald, its discoverer from the University of California, Berkeley.
facts.quote: The species name honors J. David Archibald, its discoverer, from The University of California, Berkeley.

facts.statement: In 2024, a second species, Avisaurus darwini, was named from the Hell Creek Formation, with the specific name honoring Charles Darwin.
facts.quote: In 2024, another species of Avisaurus from the Hell Creek Formation was named as Avisaurus darwini, with the specific name in honor of Charles Darwin.

facts.statement: A species originally named Avisaurus gloriae from Montana was renamed Gettyia by Atterholt et al. in 2018.
facts.quote: Avisaurus gloriae fue descubierto en la formación Dos Medicinas del Campaniano (entre 77 a 71 millones de años) de Montana, EE.UU, fue renombrado Gettyia por Atterholt et al. (2018).

facts.statement: Avisaurus fossils are found in humid low-lying swamps, lakes, and river basins along the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: Avisaurus remains fossilized in the humid low-lying swamps, lakes, and river basins of the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway, Hell Creek Formation.

facts.statement: Avisaurus possessed inwardly curved claws resembling those of eudromaeosaurs, indicating it was a predator.
facts.quote: Inwardly curved claws of the Avisaurus tarsis resemble those of eudromaeosaurs, indicating that it was predatory.

facts.statement: Avisaurus likely preyed on other vertebrates, showing similarities to modern raptors.
facts.quote: It likely preyed on other vertebrates, with similarity to some modern raptors.

facts.statement: Avisaurus belongs to the enantiornithine family Avisauridae, which includes similar animals from South America like Soroavisaurus, Neuquenornis, and Intiornis.
facts.quote: This genus belongs to the enantiornithine family Avisauridae, which also contains similar animals from South America such as Soroavisaurus, Neuquenornis and Intiornis.

facts.statement: Avisaurus fossils are known from humid low-lying swamps, lakes, and river basins on the western shore of the Niobrara Sea, as well as from drier highlands between that area and the Overthrust Belt.
facts.quote: Ambas especies de Avisaurus son conocidas de pantanos húmedos de baja altitud, lagos, y cuencas de ríos de la costa occidental del Mar de Niobrara, y de las mucho más áridas tierras altas entre esa área y la Cordillera Overthrust Belt que posteriormente formarían las Montañas Rocosas.

facts.statement: At the end of the Cretaceous, the Americas were separated by an arm of the Tethys Sea.
facts.quote: A finales del Cretácico las Américas estaban separadas por un brazo del mar de Tetis.

facts.statement: The reported presence of Avisaurus in both North and South America has been used as evidence that faunal changes in southern North America during the Lanciano were the result of an immigration event of South American taxa moving north.
facts.quote: La presencia de restos reportados de Avisaurus tanto en Norte como en Suramérica ha sido usada como evidencia de que los cambios faunísticos de la mitad sur de Norteamérica durante el Lanciano eran resultado de un evento de inmigración de taxones suramericanos moviéndose hacia el norte.

facts.statement: Avisaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
